question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should that contract be static, served at runtime, or replaced by a documented TypeBox/JSON Schema client-generation path?
rationale: This choice defines a supported external API surface with auth, endpoint visibility, versioning, and upgrade compatibility implications, so automation should not pick the contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Publish a release-attached or committed schema artifact for client generation without adding a runtime endpoint yet.

options.title: Use Existing Protocol Docs Instead
options.body: Close later only if maintainers decide the TypeBox/JSON Schema pipeline and Gateway protocol docs are the intended client-generation surface.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the closest prior OpenAPI/schema exposure work in the repository history, even though that branch was config-specific and closed unmerged.
